nodes.title: User Prompt
widgets_values:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: A 60-second bright, transparent, energetic anime-style digital-pop music video with no singing and no spoken vocals. Use <Picture 1> as the sole authoritative reference for the girl character. Preserve the exact same character identity, face, hairstyle, outfit, accessories, body proportions, and visual style from <Picture 1> throughout every shot. Do not redesign, re-costume, simplify, recolor, or reinterpret her.

The video takes place inside a huge abstract digital motion-graphics world rather than a realistic street or conventional stage. The environment is constantly evolving and filled with luminous geometric animation: expanding circles, concentric rings, triangles, hexagons, polygons, diagonal grids, floating squares, transparent panels, dot matrices, node-link networks, waveform shapes, binary digits, ribbon-like light trails, glowing lines, pixel fragments, rainbow refractions, sparkles, particle clouds, and digital shockwaves.

The girl remains the visual focus but is never locked into a static frontal composition. She performs a continuous light pop-dance performance mixed with weightless floating motion: rhythmic steps, turns, small jumps, spins, arm sweeps, reaches, shoulder movement, playful gestures, gentle kicks, midair rotations, short hover moments, and graceful drifting through the digital space.

Camera movement is highly dynamic and musical. Continuously vary viewing angle, distance, height, and orientation. Use front three-quarter views, side profiles, rear three-quarter views, high angles, low angles, overhead compositions, medium shots, full-body shots, close-ups, and occasional extreme detail cut-ins.

Actively use Push In, Pull Out, Pan, Tilt, Truck, Pedestal, Tracking Shot, Arc Shot, and limited Roll. Avoid keeping the camera perfectly frontal for more than a brief moment. Major camera movements should synchronize with musical beats, fills, rises, drops, and transition accents.

There is no lyric singing and no continuous subtitle text.

Instead, use short kinetic typography keywords as rhythmic graphic impact elements. The words do not need to form sentences or tell a story. They behave like visual percussion.

Use short words such as:
“SIGNAL”
“LINK”
“PIXEL”
“SYNC”
“BEAT”
“ZERO”
“ONE”
“CONNECT”
“LIGHT”
“ONLINE”
“WORLD”
“FLASH”
“JUMP”
“TURN”
“SPARK”
“READY?”
“NOW”
“GO!”
“SEND!”

Typography should appear suddenly and decisively, remain visible only briefly, then disappear, transform, fragment, stretch, rotate, pass through the camera, or dissolve into particles.

Do not use karaoke-style subtitles.
Do not display long text sentences.
Do not place permanent text along the bottom of the frame.

The visual intensity should evolve across the full minute:
0–15 seconds = airy digital introduction.
15–30 seconds = rhythmic expansion.
30–45 seconds = full digital spectacle.
45–54 seconds = maximum visual climax.
54–60 seconds = spacious instrumental release.

[Shot 1] Begin from a high front three-quarter angle.

The girl floats gently above a field of tiny luminous points. Large transparent cyan rings slowly rotate beneath her. Thin glowing lines form loose geometric networks in the distance.

The camera slowly Pedestals Down while performing a subtle Push In.

She raises one hand toward a floating point of light.

On a clean musical accent, the word “SIGNAL” appears sharply beside her.

“SIGNAL” expands once with a strong scale hit.

Concentric transmission rings propagate outward from the typography.

Tiny light particles travel along thin network lines.

Music cue: Airy instrumental electronic pop. Soft luminous synth pads, delicate sparkling arpeggios, restrained electronic percussion, subtle buoyant bass, and wide clean harmonic space. No vocals.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, cut to a low side three-quarter angle.

The camera performs a smooth Arc Shot around the girl while she takes two rhythmic steps and lightly rises from the implied floor.

On the beat, “LINK” appears between several glowing nodes.

Bright lines instantly connect the nodes.

The typography stretches briefly along the connection path, then breaks into small light particles.

The girl turns through the moving network and performs a light arm sweep.

Warm yellow and peach accents begin entering the blue-and-white palette.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut to an asymmetric facial close-up from a front three-quarter angle.

The camera slowly Trucks sideways.

She looks briefly toward the moving camera, blinks naturally, then glances upward.

On a sharp musical hit, “PIXEL” appears close to the lens.

The word immediately breaks into hundreds of glowing square particles.

The particles drift across her hair and face without obscuring her.

The camera Tilts Up slightly as the pixel fragments rise.

[Shot 4] At 00:10.500, emerge from the pixel cloud into a very wide rear three-quarter composition.

The girl floats forward into a much larger luminous digital space.

The camera Tracks behind her and gradually Pulls Out.

Huge transparent circles, distant grids, triangles, and glowing polygons extend deep into the background.

On a strong beat, “SYNC” slams into frame.

Several geometric rings instantly rotate into alignment around the typography.

The girl performs a small midair turn as all major graphic elements briefly synchronize their movement.

Music cue: Increase rhythmic drive. Introduce clearer drums, brighter arpeggiators, more active bass, and stronger chord movement while keeping the sound transparent and uplifting.

[Shot 5] At 00:15.000, begin the second 15-second section with a fast side Tracking Shot.

The girl moves laterally through the abstract world while floating slightly above the implied floor.

She performs:
side step → small turn → arm sweep → light kick → bounce.

The camera travels parallel to her.

Large translucent shapes pass between camera and character, creating foreground parallax.

On a heavy beat, “BEAT” rapidly Pushes directly toward the lens.

The word briefly fills most of the frame before passing through the camera and disappearing.

[Shot 6] At 00:18.500, cut to a low-angle front three-quarter composition.

The camera Pushes In as she floats upward.

She lifts one arm high and rotates gently.

Around her, glowing “0” and “1” symbols begin appearing.

On consecutive rhythmic hits:
“ZERO”
then
“ONE”

Each word appears separately.

Binary digits stream behind her at different depths.

Halfway through the shot, Arc the camera around her shoulder toward a side profile.

[Shot 7] At 00:22.000, cut overhead.

The girl spins lightly beneath the camera inside several concentric rings.

Perform a restrained Roll of approximately 20 degrees while descending toward her.

On a rhythmic fill, “CONNECT” appears large beneath her body.

Dozens of luminous nodes instantly connect into a geometric network radiating outward.

The network expands rapidly across the entire digital environment.

As the camera approaches her, she looks upward.

Cut briefly into an extreme close-up of her eyes for less than one second.

[Shot 8] At 00:26.000, snap back into a rear-side medium-wide composition.

The girl takes two quick steps across an invisible surface, jumps lightly, then becomes weightless and rotates forward.

On a bright accent, “LIGHT” appears behind her.

The word blooms into an intense white-yellow glow.

It expands into a circular flash, then transforms into thousands of floating sparkling particles.

Use soft cyan, yellow, pink, and white.

Music cue: Continue the same instrumental track seamlessly, now fuller and more energetic. Add stronger drums, brighter arpeggios, wider chords, active melodic synth lines, and a playful forward-driving bass groove.

[Shot 9] At 00:30.000, begin the third section from an extreme-wide composition.

The girl appears small inside an enormous tunnel made of rotating rings, hexagons, lines, particles, and floating transparent panels.

The camera rapidly Pushes through the tunnel toward her.

She turns toward the approaching camera and sweeps one hand across frame.

On successive beats:
“ONLINE”
then
“WORLD”

“ONLINE” flickers briefly like a digital status indicator.

“WORLD” appears enormous far behind her, embedded into the deep geometry of the environment.

The camera passes through several luminous rings as it approaches.

Music cue: Enter the full energetic digital-pop section. Strong clean electronic rhythm, bright synth hooks, dense sparkling arpeggios, lively bass movement, and wide uplifting harmony.

[Shot 10] At 00:33.500, cut to a fast side-profile Truck Shot.

The girl performs a compact dance phrase:
step → shoulder turn → hand sweep → hop → half-spin.

Large triangles and circles move rapidly across the foreground.

On a strong percussion accent, “FLASH” appears for only a fraction of a second.

The screen produces a synchronized white-cyan light burst.

Do not hold the word.

It should function like a visual impact frame.

[Shot 11] At 00:37.000, cut to a dramatic low-angle medium shot.

The camera performs an Arc Shot while the girl rises upward.

She swings one arm across the frame.

On the next musical hit, “JUMP” appears beneath her just as she launches upward.

The typography stretches vertically and disappears below frame.

Immediately afterward, “TURN” appears as she rotates in midair.

“TURN” follows a circular motion path around her and then breaks apart into curved streaks.

[Shot 12] At 00:41.000, cut to a huge overhead shot.

Hundreds of geometric objects rotate in layered circular formations.

The girl gently drops backward through the center and rotates upright.

The camera Rolls slowly in the opposite direction from the environment.

On several quick accents, small copies of “SPARK” appear around her in different positions.

Each “SPARK” creates a compact particle burst.

The bursts combine into a massive luminous spiral surrounding the girl.

Music cue: Maintain high energy and begin building toward the final climax. Add rising synth lines, stronger harmonic tension, denser arpeggios, and increasingly powerful rhythmic fills.

[Shot 13] At 00:45.000, begin the final climax section from a rear three-quarter medium-wide shot.

The girl faces a huge luminous horizon made of connected lines, rings, particles, and polygon structures.

She steps forward and rises into the air.

The camera Tracks behind her, then Arcs smoothly toward her side.

On a strong rising accent, “READY?” appears in the deep background.

The word grows larger as the camera moves.

It fragments into hundreds of geometric pieces.

The environment begins accelerating.

Music cue: Begin the major final rise. Keep the full rhythm but widen the harmony and increase melodic brightness. Strong fills should prepare the viewer for the maximum visual impact around 52–54 seconds.

[Shot 14] At 00:48.000, cut from far below looking upward.

The girl floats high above the camera.

Thousands of glowing particles rise around her against gravity.

The camera rapidly Pushes Up through the particle field.

On a sharp hit, “NOW” appears directly above her.

It remains visible for less than one second.

Immediately afterward, “GO!” slams forward toward the camera while the girl accelerates through a field of expanding rings.

Use aggressive parallax and strong forward motion.

[Shot 15] At 00:51.000, cut to an extreme close-up of one eye for only a fraction of a second.

Immediately Pull Out at high speed into a dynamic front three-quarter full-body composition.

The girl rotates, extends one hand forward, and floats toward the moving camera.

The entire digital world reaches maximum density:
rainbow refractions,
large geometric structures,
rotating rings,
pixel clouds,
node networks,
foreground streaks,
waveform bursts,
glowing ribbons,
and dense sparkling particles.

At approximately 52.5–54.0 seconds, trigger the largest typography hit in the entire video:

“SEND!”

“SEND!” appears enormous behind and partially around the girl.

On the strongest musical impact, the word explodes outward into:
hundreds of geometric fragments,
expanding concentric rings,
rainbow pixel particles,
luminous node connections,
long glowing trails,
waveform shockwaves,
and a huge digital light burst.

The girl remains clearly visible within the center of the effect.

The camera rapidly Pushes toward her hand, then instantly Pulls Out through the expanding digital explosion.

Music cue: Reach maximum instrumental intensity. Bright electronic drums, buoyant bass, wide luminous synth chords, rapid sparkling arpeggios, powerful melodic hooks, and a major synchronized impact for “SEND!”. No vocals.

[Shot 16] At 00:54.000, begin the instrumental release.

The large digital explosion continues expanding, but immediately becomes softer and more spacious.

Cut to a distant side-rear three-quarter view.

The girl floats slowly through a clean sky-blue, white, and soft rainbow environment.

Reduce the density of geometric structures.

The camera gently Trucks sideways while slowly Pulling Out.

Tiny fragments of earlier words may drift in the far background:
“SIGNAL”
“LINK”
“PIXEL”
“SYNC”
“LIGHT”

They are purely decorative fragments and should remain small and unobtrusive.

Do not introduce any new large typography.

Music cue: Remove much of the heavy rhythm. Keep shimmering synth arpeggios, warm sustained chords, soft bass resonance, delicate high electronic tones, and a gentle melodic continuation.

[Shot 17] At 00:57.000, cut to the final very wide diagonal rear-side composition.

The girl continues drifting upward and forward through an enormous open luminous space.

The camera performs a slow Pull Out with a gentle Tilt Up.

Soft particles travel past the lens at several depths, creating strong but calm parallax.

The remaining geometric structures become fewer, larger, and more distant.

One thin glowing line extends from near the girl toward the bright distant horizon.

She makes one final small turn in midair and continues drifting forward.

Do not return to a frontal pose.

Do not stop the character.

Do not display any new typography.

End naturally while both the girl and the digital space remain in gentle motion.

Music cue: Instrumental outro only. Continue soft shimmering arpeggios, sustained harmonic pads, delicate high synth tones, and minimal rhythm. Allow the arrangement to become increasingly spacious through the final frame without a heavy final impact.

Character-consistency requirement: <Picture 1> is the sole authoritative visual reference for the girl. Preserve the exact same character throughout every camera angle, including full-body views, side profiles, rear three-quarter views, high angles, low angles, overhead shots, and facial close-ups.

Performance requirement: Keep the girl continuously expressive and connected to the instrumental rhythm. Mix light dance phrases with weightless floating movement: steps, turns, reaches, spins, small jumps, body rotations, playful gestures, hover transitions, and graceful midair motion. Avoid repetitive idle swaying.

Camera-variety requirement: Do not default to a fixed frontal camera. Regularly alternate between front three-quarter, side profile, rear three-quarter, low angle, high angle, overhead, close-up, medium, full-body, and extreme-wide compositions.

Camera-motion requirement: Actively use Push In, Pull Out, Pan, Tilt, Truck, Pedestal, Tracking Shot, Arc Shot, and limited Roll. Match major camera accelerations and direction changes to musical accents.

Geometric-animation requirement: Keep the digital environment continuously evolving. Change the scale, depth, rotation, density, direction, and color of circles, rings, triangles, hexagons, grids, nodes, connecting lines, binary digits, dot matrices, floating panels, ribbons, pixels, and luminous fragments.

Particle requirement: Use abundant particles throughout, but vary their behavior. Include drifting dust, glittering sparks, pixel clouds, radial bursts, foreground streaks, orbiting particles, flowing streams, rising particles, and huge coordinated climax explosions.

Depth requirement: Maintain strong visual depth. Place some graphic elements close to the lens, some around the character, and massive structures deep in the background. Use foreground particles and typography passing the camera to create parallax.

Typography requirement: There are no lyrics and no subtitle-style text. Only short kinetic keywords are allowed. Typography acts as rhythmic visual impact and should appear suddenly, strongly, and briefly. Most words should remain visible for less than two seconds. Avoid displaying long sentences.

Typography-motion requirement: Words may slam into frame, rapidly scale, rotate, pass through the lens, stretch through depth, connect to geometric nodes, explode into particles, dissolve into pixels, trigger light flashes, or transform into environmental graphics.

Music-synchronization requirement: Synchronize character gestures, dance accents, floating changes, camera Push Ins and Pull Outs, rotations, typography hits, geometric expansions, particle bursts, light flashes, and major transitions with strong beats, fills, melodic hooks, rises, breaks, and drops.

overall_soundscape: Keep non-musical sound extremely minimal. The instrumental track dominates. Use only faint stylized digital shimmer, subtle transition sweeps, tiny sparkling accents, and soft electronic motion textures when useful.

non_diegetic_music: A continuous bright, transparent, uplifting electronic-pop instrumental track with sparkling synth arpeggios, buoyant bass, crisp electronic drums, wide luminous synth chords, rhythmic pulses, and energetic melodic hooks. No singing and no spoken vocals. Build from an airy opening into a colorful rhythmic middle section, then into a highly energetic digital-pop climax around 45–54 seconds. Use clear beats, fills, rises, drops, and accent hits so camera motion, dance gestures, particle bursts, geometric animation, and kinetic typography synchronize tightly to the music. After approximately 54 seconds, reduce the arrangement into a spacious instrumental outro with lighter drums, shimmering arpeggios, warm sustained chords, and soft high-frequency textures.
